Per-character Backspace keeps the component state in sync.

members.name: SelectFirstAvailableTimeSlotAsync
members.doc: Clicks the first available time slot regardless of the specific time value. Must exclude disabled slots explicitly — confirmed in CI (2026-07-13, 2026-07-14) that ".First" can land on an already-disabled slot (e.g. fully booked), which Playwright retries clicking for 30s and never succeeds since the parent list intercepts pointer events for disabled children. The disabled state is CSS-class-only (the underlying <input> has no `disabled` attribute — confirmed by a follow-up CI failure on 2026-07-14 after an input-attribute-based predicate didn't filter it out), so match on the label's own class instead. Returns the slot it picked (e.g. "09:00 - 10:00") so callers can assert it downstream

members.name: SuggestionsDropdown
members.doc: The autocomplete dropdown. Its CSS-module class differs between the two pages hosting this search — `FormSearchLocations_locationsList…` on /en/explore, `SearchLocations_locationsList…` on /en/explore/locations-search — so match the `SearchLocations_locationsList` substring, which is contained in both. Confirmed on UAT (2026-08-13).  Do NOT widen this to `ul[class*='locationsList']`: both pages also render five `index-module_locationsList…` region-browse blocks (120+ <li> each — one visible, four zero-size behind inactive tabs). Those hold <a> elements rather than <button>, so a `… li button` suffix excludes them today, but the bare `ul` selector matches six elements, which makes any Expect() on the dropdown itself a strict-mode violation.

members.name: AmenityCheckbox
members.doc: Amenity checkboxes have no stable id (regenerated per page load) — select by the sibling paragraph's visible label text instead. Confirmed on UAT (2026-07-10).

members.name: ResultCards

members.name: WaitForResultCountToStabilizeAsync
members.params: ILocator checkbox, int excludedCount, int timeoutMs = 15000
members.doc: A plain "wait until count != initialCount" (via WaitForFunctionAsync) can resolve on a transient/intermediate render — e.g. a brief flicker while the filtered list settles — and then revert back to the pre-click count shortly after. Confirmed live on UAT (2026-07-15): after clicking the Parking checkbox, the count can briefly differ from the baseline before settling back, causing a caller that reads the count immediately (or after a short fixed wait) to see the stale/reverted value. Poll instead: only accept a count once it's different from the baseline AND identical across two consecutive reads a short interval apart.  On timeout, the exception can't yet say WHY: it could be a genuinely slow backend/WAF response (click registered, filtering just took a while) or the click never registering at all (intercepted, stale locator after a re-render). Report the checkbox's own checked state at the timeout — that distinguishes the two next time this reproduces, instead of guessing.

members.name: TypeSearchQueryAndWaitForSuggestionsAsync
members.doc: Types a query and waits for the dropdown to actually respond, retrying the fill once — same shape as ContactFormPage.OpenCountryDropdownAsync. The search field is server-rendered and only becomes interactive once React attaches its input handler; a fill that lands in the gap between "input is visible" and "handler attached" sets the value but fires no suggestion request at all, so the dropdown stays shut and the caller waits out its full timeout. Confirmed on UAT (2026-08-13): filling immediately after the input became visible reproduced this. There is no DOM signal for "hydrated", so retype once — the second fill lands after hydration.

members.name: WaitForSearchReadyAsync
members.doc: Warm-up for tests that assert suggestions are ABSENT (e.g. "1–2 characters produce nothing"). Such an assertion passes vacuously if the field simply isn't hydrated yet — see the note on TypeSearchQueryAndWaitForSuggestionsAsync. Drive one query that is known to return results first: once the dropdown has opened, the suggestion pipeline is provably live, so a later "still closed after N ms" assertion means the app really declined to suggest.

members.name: SelectSuggestionAndWaitForNavigationAsync
members.doc: Clicks a suggestion by its exact visible text and waits for the resulting navigation to the GEO page. Exact match, not .First — several suggestions share a prefix ("Berlin, Germany" vs "Bergamo…"), and the order the backend returns them in is not ours to rely on.

members.name: SearchAndSelectLocationAsync
members.doc: Types a location and clicks its first autocomplete suggestion — same pattern as ContactFormPage.FillLocationSearchAsync. Needed so filter tests target a small, non-paginated result set deterministically instead of whatever city the runner's IP happens to geo-resolve to (a large city like London renders a fixed page of results that a filter doesn't shrink, which made ToggleAmenityFilterAsync's count-change wait time out in CI — confirmed 2026-07-13).

classes.name: LocationPage
classes.doc: Location pages such as /en/gb/london/office-space. Their hero carries an enquiry form that hands the visitor to the contact form with the location already attached, through a `#geoCountry=…&geoLocation=… &locationNumber=…&geoId=…` hash.  The hero embeds the very same contact-details widget as step 1 of the contact form — identical `#email`, `#phone` and intl-tel-input country selector — so tests drive those fields through ContactFormPage rather than duplicating its country-dropdown handling here. What is specific to the hero, and lives below, is the two-stage submit.

members.name: HeroSubmitButton
members.doc: The label is a Material Symbols text node ("arrow_right_alt") followed by "Get started" in sentence case. An exact-text XPath finds nothing; the accessible name matches case-insensitively.

members.name: ExpandHeroFormAsync
members.doc: The hero is a progressive form: on arrival only the email field is rendered, and the first click expands the form in place to reveal the phone field rather than navigating anywhere. Waiting for a navigation after a single click waits forever.

members.name: SubmitHeroFormAsync
members.doc: The second click is the one that submits. The contact form requests a token as it loads, so the wait is registered before the click — same reason as ProductPage.ClickContactFormCtaAsync.

members.name: HashParameter
members.doc: Reads one parameter out of the hash the hero handed to the contact form, so tests can assert against the location the page actually carried rather than a hardcoded centre number that would rot the day the centre closes.

classes.name: ProductPage
classes.doc: Marketing product pages such as /en/virtual-offices/business-address. Their calls to action carry the product into the contact form through a URL hash, which is what makes the form arrive preselected.

members.name: ContactFormCta
members.doc: CTAs are matched by their href rather than their label: the same `#dataProduct=…` link appears as "Get Started", "Contact Us" and "Let's talk" depending on where it sits on the page, and some cards add `&productCard=…` naming the specific sub-product card.

members.name: ClickContactFormCtaAsync
members.doc: The form POSTs for a token on load; register the wait before clicking or the response is missed — same reason ContactFormPage.NavigateToContactFormAsync does it that way.

classes.name: SolutionsPage
classes.doc: Solutions pages — /en/solutions/industry/… and /en/solutions/company-size/…. Like the product pages, their calls to action carry context into the contact form through a URL hash; an industry page sends `#industry=…`, which arrives preselected on the industry step of the sub-quiz.

members.name: ContactFormCta
members.doc: Deliberately mirrors ProductPage rather than sharing with it: Portal `BasePage` holds no helper methods at all by design, and the two page types are separate concepts. Matching on the href fragment matters here for the same reason as on product pages — every industry page also carries a plain `/en/contact-form` link with no hash, and matching on `contact-form` alone picks that one and silently loses the industry.

members.name: ClickContactFormCtaAsync
members.doc: The form requests a token as it loads; register the wait before clicking or the response is missed.

members.name: AnswerNextDialogAsync
members.doc: Answers the next browser dialog and reports its type.  Two things this has to get right. The handler is effectively `async void`, so anything thrown inside it lands on a thread-pool thread and takes the whole test host down rather than failing a test — observed on 2026-08-14, the run aborted outright. And the event is delivered asynchronously, so the caller has to await this task rather than read a field straight after the action that triggers the dialog.
